seatTerms.government: Government seats (G), including the Government share in private colleges
seatTerms.management: Private (GMP, OPN, minority) and Others (Q) seats

process.title: Check which eligibility clause you fit
process.description: Before you apply, confirm you meet one of the eligibility clauses (a, b, c, d, e, f, g, y or z) on the KEA website. You enter its clause code in the application. The fee isn't refunded for any reason.

process.title: Create your profile online
process.description: Register on the KEA PGET 2026 portal with your NEET-PG 2026 or NEET-MDS 2026 roll number. Your name, parents' names, date of birth, NBE score and mobile number are fetched from NBE data. An OTP goes to the mobile number you registered with NBE. Don't share it.

process.title: Fill in the application
process.description: Applications are online only; offline or postal forms aren't accepted. Enter your eligibility clause code, reservation category, educational qualification and contact details. In-service candidates enter their in-service details. Upload your photograph, left thumb impression and signature.

process.title: Pay the registration fee
process.description: Pay online through the payment gateway: ₹750 for SC/ST/Category-1/PwD, ₹1,500 for General/2A/2B/3A/3B, ₹4,000 for non-Karnataka candidates and ₹7,000 for NRI/OCI/PIO/foreign national candidates.

process.title: Check, declare and print
process.description: Until you select the declaration, you can edit the form any number of times and take draft printouts. Once you declare, nothing can be changed. Take the final printout and keep your application ID and password private.

process.title: Get your documents verified at KEA
process.description: Clause a and clause y candidates don't need to attend, unless they claim NRI Ward or religious minority reservation. Everyone else books a slot on the KEA website and attends in person at KEA, 18th Cross, Sampige Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, with originals and two sets of photocopies. You get a documents verification slip, which you need to enter options. KEA has published these steps for PG Dental (NEET MDS); confirm the PG Medical arrangements with KEA.

process.title: Enter your options, then check the mock allotment
process.description: Enter your college and course options in order of priority. The same list is used for Rounds 1 and 2; the mop-up round needs fresh options. A mock allotment shows an indicative result. You can then add, delete or reorder options until the last date for real allotment.

process.title: Round 1: see your allotment and pick a choice
process.description: Log in after the Round 1 result and select one of four choices. If you don't select one, your seat is cancelled automatically and you can't take part in later rounds.

process.title: Pay, submit originals and join
process.description: Pay the fees, submit your original documents to KEA, collect the admission order and report to the college by the last date on it. Then update your joining status on the KEA portal and ask the college to enter your reporting details on its portal.

process.title: Later rounds
process.description: After Round 1 come Round 2, Round 3 (mop-up) and the stray vacancy round. KEA publishes the rules, instructions and schedule for each round on its website.

listedHomeInstitutions.label: None: clause a covers any recognised medical or dental institution in Karnataka
listedHomeInstitutions.note: The bulletin doesn't single out any Karnataka institution (unlike AMU/BHU/AIIMS in UP).

inServiceLabel.label: In-service candidate under the Government / DME of Karnataka (detailed in-service guidelines will be published later)

rules.title: Qualified in NEET-PG 2026 or NEET-MDS 2026
rules.explanation: Only candidates who scored at least the prescribed minimum in NEET-PG 2026 (MD/MS/Diploma) or NEET-MDS 2026 (MDS) can register. Qualifying alone doesn't give you a right to a seat. You must also meet the eligibility conditions and complete registration, including document verification.

rules.title: NEET-MDS 2026 qualifying cut-offs
rules.explanation: NBEMS cut-offs (out of 960): General/EWS 50th percentile, 308; General PwBD 45th percentile, 289; SC/ST/OBC (including their PwBD) 40th percentile, 271. Non-Karnataka candidates (including PwD) need the General (UR) 50th percentile: 308.

rules.title: PG Medical rules take effect after MCC's announcement
rules.explanation: This bulletin covers PG Medical and Dental, but its information about PG Medical comes into effect only after MCC announces it. Watch the KEA website for the PG Medical notice and schedule.
rules.note: Document verification slot booking is announced only for PG Dental (p66, p67).

rules.title: MDS: internship by 31st May 2026
rules.explanation: For NEET-MDS 2026, the NBEMS cut-off date for completing your internship is 31st May 2026.
rules.note: p20 (item 9) accepts a provisional internship certificate for candidates 'completing their internship 31st March 2026 for MDS', which doesn't match the 31st May 2026 cut-off on p7. Confirm with KEA.

rules.title: MD/MS/Diploma: internship cut-off as set by NMC/NBEMS
rules.explanation: For NEET-PG 2026, the internship cut-off follows NMC/NBEMS. This bulletin doesn't state the date. A provisional internship completion certificate (Annexure 6) is accepted for the first round only.

rules.title: Already hold a clinical PG degree
rules.explanation: If you already hold a PG degree in any clinical specialty, you are not eligible for admission to any PG degree or diploma course.

rules.title: MBBS/BDS in Karnataka with 10 years of school in Karnataka (clause b)
rules.explanation: You fit clause b: as on 31st March 2026 you studied at least 10 academic years (1st to 12th standard) in government or government-recognised institutions in Karnataka, passed SSLC/10th or 2nd PUC/12th there, and passed MBBS/BDS in Karnataka. A class you took more than one year to pass counts as one year. You're eligible for Government, GMP, OPN and Others (Q) seats, and minority seats if you qualify.

rules.title: MBBS/BDS outside Karnataka with 10 years of school in Karnataka (clause c)
rules.explanation: You fit clause c: you studied at least 10 academic years (1st to 12th standard) in Karnataka, passed SSLC/10th or 2nd PUC/12th there, and passed MBBS/BDS from a recognised institution in India outside Karnataka. A class you took more than one year to pass counts as one year. You're eligible for Government, GMP, OPN and Others (Q) seats, and minority seats if you qualify.

rules.title: MBBS/BDS in Karnataka without 10 years of school there (clause a)
rules.explanation: You fit clause a: an Indian citizen who passed MBBS/BDS in Karnataka. That makes you eligible for Government seats, OPN seats and Others (Q) seats. GMP seats and the Karnataka religious and linguistic minority seats need 10 years of school in Karnataka (clause b/c), so they aren't open to you, though Christian or Muslim candidates may get religious-minority seats left after Karnataka candidates. If clause d (a parent in the All India Service, Karnataka cadre, posted outside the state) or clause f (years in New Delhi while your parent was an MP from Karnataka) lets you count years outside Karnataka, answer 'Yes, in Karnataka' to the 10-year question.

rules.title: MBBS/BDS outside Karnataka without 10 years of school there (clause y)
rules.explanation: Government seats need MBBS/BDS in Karnataka (clause a) or 10 years of school in Karnataka (clause b/c), and GMP seats need clause b/c. As an Indian citizen who passed MBBS/BDS outside Karnataka, you can apply for OPN seats (open to all Indian citizens) and Others (Q) seats. If you're a Christian or Muslim candidate, religious-minority seats left after Karnataka candidates are offered may also come to you. If you qualify under clause d, e, f or g (see 'Other routes'), Government seats may be open to you too. Confirm with KEA.

rules.title: MBBS/BDS from outside India
rules.explanation: You must have passed the FMGE screening test, be registered with MCI/DCI (or a State Medical Council) and complete your internship by the prescribed date. Government seats appear to need MBBS/BDS from India (clause a or c), and Others (Q) seats need a college affiliated to a university in India, so only OPN seats and, if you qualify, NRI seats appear to be open. If you studied 10 years in Karnataka, clause c's table row (which only says MBBS/BDS 'from outside the State of Karnataka') could open Government and GMP seats too. Confirm with KEA.
rules.note: Interpretation: 8.1(c) says MBBS/BDS 'located in India' for Government seats, and 8.4 says Q seats need a college affiliated to a university in India. The clause c row in the table (p16) only says 'outside the State of Karnataka'. Clause y's wording ('outside the state of Karnataka') could include abroad.

rules.title: NRI seats are for NRIs and their children or wards
rules.explanation: NRI seats are for NRIs, children or wards of NRIs, PIOs, OCIs and foreign nationals. You told us no one is an NRI for your application, so NRI seats aren't open to you unless an NRI relative sponsors you as a ward (relationship as per the Supreme Court order in W.P.(c) No. 689/2017). Confirm with KEA.
rules.note: The profile asks whether you or your parents are NRIs. Karnataka also accepts NRI wards sponsored by other relatives, which the profile doesn't capture.

rules.title: NRI seats: sponsor documents needed
rules.explanation: NRIs, children of NRIs and NRI wards can apply for NRI seats (15% of seats in KPCF, KRLMPCA, AMPCK and private university colleges). If you claim NRI Ward (as an NRI's child or ward), you need the Ward Certificate (Annexure 17), the sponsor's NRI/OCI status certificate from the Indian Consulate issued within the last 6 months (Annexure 17(A)), a family tree signed by a Tahsildar, and copies of the sponsor's bank passbook, passport and visa. Others (Q) seats aren't open to NRI, PIO, OCI or foreign national candidates: if you yourself are the NRI (not just your parents), don't count on Q seats. 'NRI' here means an individual resident outside India who is an Indian citizen or a PIO, including OCIs (Income Tax Act 1961, sections 115C(e) and 6).

rules.title: OCI, PIO and foreign national candidates (clause z)
rules.explanation: OCI, PIO, NRI and foreign national candidates apply under clause z. Government, GMP and OPN seats need Indian citizenship, and Others (Q) seats exclude NRI, PIO, OCI and foreign nationals, so only NRI seats are open to OCI and foreign national candidates.

rules.title: Foreign nationals: registration
rules.explanation: Your qualification must be registered with the registering authority of the country where you got your basic medical degree, and recognised by that country's medical council. Get a temporary registration certificate from MCI/DCI for the course, within one month of securing admission.

rules.title: Reservation is for Karnataka candidates only
rules.explanation: SC/ST/OBC reservation applies only to Karnataka SC/ST/OBC candidates. Non-Karnataka candidates aren't eligible for reservation, and must score at least the General (UR) qualifying cut-off (50th percentile) to register. The bulletin doesn't define 'Karnataka candidate'; we've used your domicile. Confirm with KEA.
rules.note: Interpretation: the bulletin doesn't define 'Karnataka candidate'. Reservation certificates are issued by Karnataka Tahsildars, so non-Karnataka domicile is used here. The bulletin's only working definition (p18: minority candidates of clause b/c count as Karnataka) would point to 10 years of schooling instead. Confirm with KEA.

rules.title: EWS: confirm reservation and registration fee
rules.explanation: The NBEMS qualifying cut-off table includes General/EWS. No separate EWS registration rate or Karnataka EWS reservation rule is listed in this bulletin. Confirm the applicable fee group and reservation treatment with KEA.

rules.title: SC candidates: SCA, SCB or SCC certificate
rules.explanation: Karnataka has internal reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCA, SCB and SCC). Get a caste certificate with your SCA, SCB or SCC group printed on it and enter its RD number when you apply. Otherwise you can't select seats reserved for Scheduled Castes. The bulletin doesn't define a Karnataka SC candidate; we go by your domicile, so confirm with KEA if that differs from where your certificate was issued.

rules.title: PwD: medical examination at KEA
rules.explanation: PwD reservation is for Karnataka candidates only. Eligibility for benchmark disabilities follows the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (see the MCC PH notice on the KEA site). Every PwD candidate must attend a medical examination at KEA on the notified dates. If you're found not eligible under the Act, you'll be disqualified at any stage of admission.

rules.title: PwD reservation is for Karnataka candidates only
rules.explanation: PwD reservation applies to Karnataka candidates only, so you'd compete without PwD seats and need the General (UR) cut-off. The bulletin doesn't define 'Karnataka candidate'; we've used your domicile. Confirm with KEA.
rules.note: Interpretation: 'Karnataka candidates' read as Karnataka domicile, as for caste reservation.

rules.title: In-service candidates
rules.explanation: Detailed in-service guidelines, eligibility conditions and procedures will be published later, after KEA receives them from the Government/DME. Rule 9 of the MCI PG Medical Education Regulations, 2000 and in-service subject restrictions will apply. You pay the full fees and claim reimbursement from your department, and at admission you sign a bond to serve the Government for at least 10 years.

rules.title: Parent-service route (clauses d, e, f and g)
rules.explanation: You said a parent's service gives you a Karnataka route. Clauses d, e, f and g open Government seats, along with OPN, NRI and Others (Q) seats. GMP seats need clause b or c: only clause d lets you count the years you studied outside Karnataka during your parent's posting toward the 10 years, so under clause d GMP seats may open too. Check you meet every condition of your clause (see Other routes) and bring its certificates. Confirm with KEA.

rules.title: Other routes: clauses d, e, f and g
rules.explanation: Some candidates can count study outside Karnataka or don't need the 10 years. Clause d: children of a serving All India Service officer of the Karnataka cadre can count the years they studied outside Karnataka while the parent served outside Karnataka toward the 10 years under clause b or c. Clause e: children of an employee of the Union Government, or of a Union or Karnataka State Government undertaking or joint sector undertaking, if the parent declared a Karnataka home town on joining service, studied at least 10 years in Karnataka, and was or is liable to transfer anywhere in India. You can have passed the qualifying exam anywhere in India. The employer's certificate must show the parent is transferable, so if your parent has left service, confirm with KEA. Clause f: children of MPs elected from Karnataka, for years studied in New Delhi during the MP's tenure. Clause g: children of serving defence personnel or ex-servicemen who declared a Karnataka home town on joining; the qualifying exam can be from anywhere in India. These are routes to Government seats; the bulletin ties GMP seats only to clauses b and c. 'Children' means natural-born sons or daughters, not adopted children or grandchildren.

rules.title: Hyderabad-Karnataka (Kalyana Karnataka) reservation, Article 371(j)
rules.explanation: If you're a local person of the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, you can claim reservation under Article 371(j) with a certificate from the Assistant Commissioner (Annexure 8). Seat searches follow the category-specific order in the brochure’s chart. They start with General Merit (GM), then Hyderabad-Karnataka GM (GMH); some categories then search the non-HK category before the HK category. For SCH, the chart gives GM → GMH → SCG → SCH.

rules.title: Christian and Muslim minority seats
rules.explanation: Christian and Muslim candidates of clause b/c count as Karnataka religious minority candidates. After the Karnataka list is exhausted, leftover seats go to other eligible religious-minority candidates, including non-Karnataka ones. You need a religious minority certificate from the Tahsildar (Annexure 12).

rules.title: Linguistic minority seats (Tamil, Telugu, Kodava, Tulu)
rules.explanation: Linguistic minority seats are for Karnataka candidates whose mother tongue is Tamil, Telugu, Kodava or Tulu, and who studied at least 10 academic years (1st to 12th standard) in Karnataka, passing SSLC/10th or 2nd PUC/12th there. You need a linguistic minority certificate countersigned by the BEO or Deputy Director, PU (Annexure 9/10).

rules.title: St. John's Medical College, Bengaluru
rules.explanation: St. John's has four categories: (1) Roman Catholic religious nuns with SJMC-approved two-year rural service, (2) SJMC alumni with SJMC-approved two-year rural service, (3) Roman Catholic Christians, (4) general open merit. Categories 1 to 3 need their own certificates (Annexures 13 to 16). The bulletin lists no extra certificate for general open merit.

rules.title: You must swear you hold no other PG admission
rules.explanation: Every candidate signs the Annexure 7 affidavit, declaring they haven't taken PG admission in any college allotted by other exam-conducting bodies and haven't surrendered a seat in past NEET-PG/NEET-MDS or other state PG entrance counselling. The wording about which past exams count is unclear. If you can't truthfully declare this, check with KEA before applying. A false declaration means losing the seat and criminal proceedings.
rules.note: The affidavit's wording ('past NEET-PG 2026 / NEET MDS 2026 exams') is garbled, so how far back 'surrendered' reaches is uncertain.

rules.title: Cancelled a PG seat or didn't join? 3-year bar
rules.explanation: If, as a regular (non-in-service) candidate, you cancelled or surrendered a PG Medical/Dental seat after the last date of admissions, you're not eligible for a management quota or any other PG seat for three years. If you fail to join after allotment, the same three-year bar and disciplinary action apply, and this proviso appears to cover in-service candidates too.
rules.note: Wording on p44 is run-on; this restates both provisos. Check the original.

terms.meaning: State-quota seats in government colleges, and the government's share of seats in private colleges.
Private-college seats for candidates under clause b or c (10 years of school in Karnataka).
Open private-college seats, filled on NEET All India merit, for any Indian citizen.
15% of seats in private colleges, for NRIs, their children or wards, PIOs, OCIs and foreign nationals.
10% of seats in private colleges (5% in private universities), open to all qualified candidates except NRI, PIO, OCI and foreign national candidates.

manualReview.title: Confirm the full Karnataka eligibility requirements
manualReview.detail: Your profile does not establish NEET qualification, a previously completed clinical PG degree, the cancellation/non-joining bar or every affidavit and quota condition. The bulletin does not define Karnataka candidacy as domicile, and its PG Medical rules take effect after MCC's announcement. Confirm these requirements and any NRI route with KEA.

rules.title: Four types of seats
rules.detail: Seats are Government (G), Private (P), NRI (N) and Others (Q). Government seats are 50% of seats in government colleges (the other 50% go to All India Quota through MCC), 33% in private non-minority colleges, 20% in private minority colleges and 40% in private university colleges.

rules.title: Private seats: GMP and OPN
rules.detail: In KPCF colleges, 42% of seats are private quota: half are GMP seats (GMPH in Hyderabad-Karnataka colleges) and half are OPN seats, filled on NEET-PG All India merit and open only to Indian citizens. In KRLMPCA and AMPCK colleges, 55% are private quota: 66% go to religious or linguistic minority candidates and the other 34% are split equally between GMP and OPN. In private universities, 40% are private quota.

rules.title: NRI and Others (Q) seats
rules.detail: NRI seats are 15% of seats in KPCF, KRLMPCA, AMPCK and private university colleges. Others (Q) seats are 10% in KPCF, KRLMPCA and AMPCK colleges and 5% in private universities.

rules.title: Reservation for Karnataka candidates only
rules.detail: SC/ST/OBC reservation applies only to Karnataka SC/ST/OBC candidates. Non-Karnataka candidates aren't eligible for reservations, though non-Karnataka Christian and Muslim candidates can get religious-minority seats left after Karnataka candidates.

rules.title: SC internal reservation: SCA, SCB, SCC
rules.detail: Karnataka SC candidates need a caste certificate with SCA, SCB or SCC printed on it, and must enter its RD number when applying. Without it, you can't select seats reserved for Scheduled Castes.

rules.title: How category seats are searched
rules.detail: For every option, the computer first looks for a General Merit (GM) seat, then your category seat (e.g. SC: GM, then SCG). Hyderabad-Karnataka candidates go through more steps (e.g. SCH: GM, GMH, SCG, then SCH), and PwD candidates through longer chains that include PWD seats. This improves your allotment as per the roster. The bulletin's text says GMH is checked after GM for every category, but its chart shows GMH only for Hyderabad-Karnataka candidates.
rules.note: The prose on p31 says GMH is searched for any category; the table on the same page shows GMH only for Hyderabad-Karnataka (H) categories. Follows the table.

rules.title: Your category can't be changed later
rules.detail: The caste/category, annual income and other reservation details you enter stay the same for verification and allotment. No change is allowed later for any reason.

rules.title: Caste certificate forms
rules.detail: Caste or caste-income certificates come from the Tahsildar: Form-D for SC/ST, Form-E for Category-1, and Form-F for 2A, 2B, 3A and 3B. A married woman's certificate must be in her name with her husband's name and the spouse's income. Caste, income and 371(j) certificates must be in the name of the candidate and father.

rules.title: PwD reservation
rules.detail: PwD reservation is for Karnataka candidates only, as per the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Every PwD candidate must attend the medical examination at KEA on the notified dates.

registration.covers: For General, 2A, 2B, 3A and 3B candidates. SC/ST/Category-1/PwD pay ₹750, non-Karnataka candidates ₹4,000, and NRI/OCI/PIO/foreign national candidates ₹7,000. Paid online through the payment gateway.

rules.title: Registration fee depends on who you are
rules.detail: ₹750 for SC/ST/Category-1/PwD candidates, ₹1,500 for General/2A/2B/3A/3B, ₹4,000 for non-Karnataka candidates and ₹7,000 for NRI/OCI/PIO/foreign national candidates.

rules.title: Fees aren't refunded
rules.detail: Confirm you meet an eligibility clause before applying. The fee you pay won't be refunded for any reason.

rules.title: Missed option entry before the mock? ₹750 to enter options
rules.detail: Eligible candidates who didn't enter options for the mock allotment can still enter options by registering and paying a non-refundable fee of ₹750.

rules.title: Check the fee structure before choosing
rules.detail: The Government's seat matrix and fee structure are put on the KEA website. Check the fees, seat type and college location of each course before entering options, and discuss them with your parents.

rules.title: SC/ST fee exemption (Karnataka candidates)
rules.detail: On Government seats (codes ending in G): annual income below ₹2.50 lakh, no fees; above ₹2.50 lakh and below ₹10 lakh, pay 50% of the tuition fee. On Private seats (codes ending in P), you pay the full fees. The bulletin isn't clear about an income of exactly ₹2.50 lakh; confirm with the concerned department.
rules.note: The paragraph below the table says SC/ST candidates are exempt 'if their annual income is Rupees 2.50 lakhs'. The table says 'below'.

rules.title: Category-1 fee exemption (Karnataka candidates)
rules.detail: With annual income below ₹2.5 lakh: no fees for seats in government colleges. For Government-quota seats in private colleges, the government-college fee is deducted from what you pay. On Private seats (P), you pay the fees. Contact the concerned department about exemption and reimbursement criteria.

rules.title: OBC: pay first, claim reimbursement
rules.detail: Other Backward Class candidates pay the fees to KEA and can apply to the Backward Classes Department for reimbursement after admission.

rules.title: In-service candidates pay full fees
rules.detail: All in-service candidates pay the full fees and get reimbursed by their department as per deputation rules.

rules.title: NRI sponsor payments
rules.detail: If an NRI sponsor pays your fees, follow the separate instructions on the KEA website for payment by an NRI sponsor.

rules.title: NRI and Others (Q) seats: bank guarantee
rules.detail: Students on NRI and Others (Q) seats must give the college a bank guarantee for the balance course period, at admission or within the time the college allows. Otherwise the admission is cancelled or classes are suspended until it's provided.

calculationNote.title: Confirm your registration-fee group
calculationNote.detail: The bulletin lists ₹750 for SC/ST/Category-1/PwD, ₹1,500 for General/2A/2B/3A/3B, ₹4,000 for non-Karnataka candidates and ₹7,000 for NRI/OCI/PIO/foreign nationals. Registration fees are non-refundable. Confirm the applicable group with KEA where these descriptions overlap; the profile does not establish every category or Karnataka-candidate criterion.

choiceFilling.title: One option list for Rounds 1 and 2
choiceFilling.detail: You enter options once. The same priority list is used for the first and second rounds, and you can't enter options again. After a round you can only delete or reorder them. You must declare before you can start option entry.

choiceFilling.title: Enter options even where no seats are shown
choiceFilling.detail: Seats can come back from All India Quota surrenders, new intake approvals and new courses, and consequential vacancies arise during allotment. Enter every option you want in priority order, whatever the number of seats shown.

choiceFilling.title: The mock allotment is only indicative
choiceFilling.detail: After option entry, a mock allotment shows the seat you might get, with college-, course- and category-wise mock cut-off ranks. You don't report to a college. Use it to add, delete or reorder options before the last date. The real allotment can differ because others change their options too.

choiceFilling.title: No seat in the mock? Add more options
choiceFilling.detail: If you weren't allotted a seat in the mock allotment, check your options and add more you're interested in.

choiceFilling.title: Options lock at the deadline
choiceFilling.detail: Enter your final options before the last date and time. You can't change them after that. Keep a printout of your final options.

choiceFilling.title: You can't refuse a seat you opted for
choiceFilling.detail: Seats are allotted strictly by merit and your options. You can't claim ignorance or reject an allotted seat, so list only colleges and courses you'll actually join.

choiceFilling.title: Verification slip needed
choiceFilling.detail: You can enter options only after online registration, payment and document verification at KEA, which gives you the documents verification slip. Clause a and clause y candidates are excused from attending verification, but the bulletin doesn't say how they get the slip. Confirm with KEA.
choiceFilling.note: p67 says clause a and clause y candidates need not attend verification (unless claiming NRI Ward or religious minority). The bulletin doesn't say how they get the slip.

rounds.title: Two rounds, then mop-up and stray
rounds.detail: Counselling has Round 1, Round 2, Round 3 (mop-up) and a stray vacancy round. Allotment follows merit, your options and the Government roster. Eligibility for each round is subject to MCC's conditions.

rounds.title: Every round is online, run by KEA
rounds.detail: As per the NMC letter dated 24th July 2023, all rounds, including the stray vacancy round, are conducted online by KEA only.

rounds.title: Not reporting counts as seat blocking
rounds.detail: If you're allotted a seat in any round, you must report to the college. Not reporting isn't treated as surrendering the seat: it's seat blocking, which attracts a penalty, and the Government may take legal action.

rounds.title: Getting your originals back
rounds.detail: If you surrender a seat after results, originals are returned only after you pay the penalty. Candidates without a seat get originals back on request, collected in person with the original verification slip and ID card.

rounds.title: Pick one of four choices
rounds.detail: After the Round 1 result, log in and select one of four choices. If you don't, or don't follow the prescribed procedure, your seat is cancelled automatically and you can't take part in further rounds.

rounds.title: Choice 1: accept and quit counselling
rounds.detail: You're fully satisfied and won't take part in later rounds. Pay the fees, submit originals, collect the admission order, report to the college by the last date, and update your joining status on the KEA portal. If you don't report back to KEA that you joined, your seat is cancelled even if you physically joined.

rounds.title: Choice 1 but didn't join? Fees forfeited
rounds.detail: If you pay and get the admission order but don't report by the last date, no extension is given. The allotment is cancelled, you aren't considered in later rounds, and the fees you paid are forfeited. Failing to produce originals or pay the fees also cancels the seat.

rounds.title: Choice 2: keep the seat, try to upgrade
rounds.detail: Pay the fees for your Round 1 seat and submit originals as scheduled. In Round 2 your current seat becomes your last option and only higher options are tried. If you get a higher one, your old seat is cancelled automatically. If not, you keep it. You can't choose between them, and you must take admission. No admission order is given at this stage.

rounds.title: Choice 2: to keep your seat, delete higher options
rounds.detail: All your higher options appear on screen. To keep your Round 1 seat, delete them all. Only keep options better than your seat.

rounds.title: Choice 3: give up the seat, try again
rounds.detail: Surrender your Round 1 seat and take part in Round 2 with your other options. You don't pay fees for the Round 1 seat, but you must submit originals or you can't take part. If Round 2 allots nothing, you have no seat.

rounds.title: Choice 4: quit
rounds.detail: You're not satisfied, have a seat elsewhere, and quit. Your seat is cancelled and you can't take part in later rounds.

rounds.title: Round 2: originals are mandatory
rounds.detail: To take part in Round 2, Choice 2 and Choice 3 candidates and those without a Round 1 seat must submit originals (verification slip, all originals including Annexures 1, 2 and 7, and one set of photocopies) as scheduled. Choice 2 candidates must also have paid the fees.

rounds.title: Exited AIQ Round 2? You can join Round 2
rounds.detail: If you were allotted a seat in All India Quota or Deemed University Round 2, didn't join and exited with the forfeiture clause, you can take part in Karnataka's Round 2 after depositing originals at KEA.

rounds.title: Who can't take part in Round 2
rounds.detail: Candidates who didn't enter options for Round 1, didn't exercise a choice, Choice 2 candidates who didn't pay or deposit originals, Choice 3 or unallotted candidates who didn't deposit originals, and Choice 1/2 candidates who cancelled or surrendered.

rounds.title: Round 2: reorder, but no new options
rounds.detail: You can reorder or delete options after confirming fees, but adding new options isn't permitted. Keep options even if no seats are shown, because vacancies arise during allotment. A vacancy that arises after your turn can't be claimed. Seats freed when Choice 2 candidates upgrade (virtual vacancies) go to the next candidate who kept that option.

rounds.title: Round 2: no choices, joining is compulsory
rounds.detail: There are no choices after Round 2. If you're allotted a seat, pay the fees (Choice 2 fees are adjusted) and report to the college by the last date. Taking admission is compulsory.

rounds.title: Not joining a Round 2 seat means legal action
rounds.detail: If you don't report to the college after a Round 2 allotment, legal action will be initiated against you.

rounds.title: Got a better seat elsewhere? Surrender before Round 2
rounds.detail: If you joined (Choice 1) or paid (Choice 2) and may take a seat from another board, surrender your seat to KEA on or before the last date for Round 2 option entry, so it goes to another candidate.

rounds.title: Round 3: upgrade while admitted
rounds.detail: As per recent High Court orders, candidates admitted to a Round 2 seat (or any KEA seat they joined) can take part in Round 3 for an upgrade. If you get nothing, your earlier seat stays confirmed.

rounds.title: Who can take part in the mop-up
rounds.detail: Candidates with no seat after KEA Round 2, and those who joined a KEA-allotted college. Not eligible: those allotted a seat who didn't exercise a choice in Round 1, didn't pay or didn't report, and anyone who joined a college through All India (including deemed university) counselling or any other board. This All India rule follows the MCC bulletin and is subject to any conditions set by the Government of India.

rounds.title: Mop-up: enter options afresh
rounds.detail: Only candidates holding the verification slip who deposit originals can enter options. Earlier options are ignored, so enter fresh ones, only for colleges and courses you'll join after checking fees.

rounds.title: Mop-up: a new seat cancels the old one
rounds.detail: If you're allotted a seat in this round, your earlier seat is cancelled automatically and you can't get it back. You must report to the newly allotted college.

rounds.title: After mop-up: join and update KEA
rounds.detail: There are no choices. Pay the fees (if not paid), report to the college by the last date on the admission order and update your details through your KEA login, or you lose the seat. Not reporting means legal action.

rounds.title: Stray vacancy round eligibility
rounds.detail: Only candidates who haven't been allotted any PG Medical/Dental seat by KEA in any round can take part. Those who reported to a college after MCC, deemed university or any other allotment in the three rounds, and those allotted a seat in MCC's stray vacancy round, aren't eligible.

rounds.title: Missing or fake originals
rounds.detail: If any original certificate isn't produced during verification, or is false, concocted or a colour photocopy, you're disqualified from further allotment and liable for criminal prosecution.

documents.name: KEA PGET-2026 registration form (printout)
Photo identity and address proof
documents.detail: PAN card, driving licence, voter ID, passport, Aadhaar card or ration card.

documents.name: NEET-PG 2026 / NEET-MDS 2026 admit card and score card
documents.detail: NEET-MDS scorecards can be downloaded from natboard.edu.in for only 6 months from 10th June 2026.

documents.name: SSLC / 10th standard marks card (for date of birth)
2nd PUC / 12th standard marks card
MBBS/BDS marks cards for all phases/years
Qualifying degree certificate
documents.detail: Clause a and b candidates: stating you studied MBBS/BDS in Karnataka. A provisional degree, pass or completion certificate is accepted only if you passed MBBS/BDS in 2026.

documents.name: Qualifying degree certificate stating you studied MBBS/BDS outside Karnataka (clause y)
documents.note: p25 says a PDC/pass/completion certificate is accepted only for candidates who passed 'during 2021', probably a typo for 2026.
documents.detail: For this clause the bulletin says a provisional, pass or completion certificate is accepted only if you passed in 2021; for other clauses it says 2026. Confirm the year with KEA before relying on a provisional certificate.

documents.name: Internship completion certificate (Annexure 5)
documents.detail: A provisional internship completion certificate (Annexure 6) is accepted for the first round only. For MDS the bulletin gives two dates (31st March 2026 here, 31st May 2026 as the cut-off), so confirm with KEA; for MD/MS it follows NBEMS.
documents.note: Annexures 5 and 6 are worded for MBBS (Karnataka Medical Council), but BDS candidates need them too. The 31st March 2026 MDS date doesn't match the 31st May 2026 cut-off on p7.

documents.name: Certificate from your college head that it's recognised by MCI/DCI
State/Central Medical or Dental Council registration certificate
documents.detail: Provisional registration is accepted only if you passed in 2026. You must submit the permanent certificate at admission. If you passed before 2026, you must have and upload the original permanent registration. Foreign nationals are also asked for home-country registration and temporary MCI/DCI registration within one month of admission; confirm with KEA how this rule applies to you.

documents.name: Eligibility certificate from RGUHS (if your degree is from a university other than RGUHS)
documents.detail: Submitted at the college you're admitted to.

documents.name: Migration certificate (if MBBS/BDS isn't from RGUHS)
documents.detail: Submitted at the college you're admitted to.

documents.name: Affidavit (Annexure 7) on white paper, and on ₹100 e-stamp paper in your name
documents.detail: Needed at verification, and deposited again before Round 2. You swear you haven't taken PG admission elsewhere, haven't surrendered a seat, will notify KEA immediately if you get admission elsewhere, and will surrender only at KEA. You become eligible for admission and allotment only once you submit it.

documents.name: Compulsory rural service bond (Annexure 1) on ₹100 stamp paper, notarised, with the personal details sheet
documents.detail: Submitted when you collect the admission order at KEA. The form is written for non-in-service PG Medical candidates, so if you're in-service or taking MDS, confirm with KEA.
documents.note: Annexure 1 is titled 'for non in-service Candidates' and written for PG Medical admissions, but section 8.5.1 lists it as mandatory for all candidates, and Choice 2/3 candidates deposit it before Round 2.

documents.name: Bond to pay ₹10,00,000 (degree) or ₹4,00,000 (diploma) if you leave the course
documents.detail: In the form specified by the Government. Lower amounts apply to pre-clinical and para-clinical seats.

documents.name: Bond to serve the Government for at least 10 years
Three-year service undertaking (Annexure 2) on ₹200 stamp paper, notarised, with two sureties
documents.detail: For Government seats in PG medical courses. Attach self-attested PAN and Aadhaar copies of both sureties.
documents.note: Section 8.5.1 lists Annexure 2 as mandatory for everyone; the undertaking text covers Government seats in PG medical courses.

documents.name: FMGE screening test pass certificate
Caste / caste-income certificate from the Tahsildar (Form-D, E or F)
documents.detail: Form-D for SC/ST, Form-E for Category-1, Form-F for 2A, 2B, 3A and 3B. SC candidates need SCA, SCB or SCC printed on it, with the RD number.

documents.name: Article 371(j) Hyderabad-Karnataka certificate (Annexure 8), if you claim it
Study certificate for 10 years (1st to 12th standard) in Karnataka (Annexure 11)
documents.detail: From the head of each institution, countersigned by the BEO/DDPI for 1st to 10th standard. 11th and 12th need only the principal's or a gazetted officer's seal and signature.

documents.name: SSLC/10th or 2nd PUC/12th marks card showing you studied and passed in Karnataka
If you claim NRI Ward: Ward Certificate (Annexure 17) and sponsor's NRI/OCI status certificate (Annexure 17(A))
documents.detail: The sponsor must have stayed abroad for more than 182 days in the last financial year; the Consulate status certificate is valid for six months. Also bring a family tree signed by a Tahsildar (notary-signed or a relationship affidavit isn't accepted), a Consulate certificate issued within the last 6 months naming you and the sponsor (notary-signed isn't accepted), and copies of the sponsor's bank passbook, passport and visa. An e-copy may be accepted for verification if you submit the original at admission.

documents.name: Parents' residence certificate from the embassy (or affidavit on ₹100 e-stamp paper), passport/visa, proof of citizenship and income tax documents
documents.detail: Also the sponsor's Embassy/Consulate certificate issued within the last 6 months, and a study certificate for studies outside India where applicable. NRI and PIO candidates under clause z need these too.
documents.note: The profile can't identify NRI/PIO candidates themselves, so this is shown only for OCI and foreign nationals.

documents.name: Registration certificate from your home country's medical council
documents.detail: Then get temporary registration from MCI/DCI within one month of admission.

documents.name: Religious minority certificate from the Tahsildar (Annexure 12), if you claim it
documents.detail: Karnataka minority candidates also need the 10-year study certificate.

documents.name: Linguistic minority certificate (Annexure 9 or 10), if you claim it
documents.detail: Countersigned by the BEO (1st to 10th) or Deputy Director, PU (11th and 12th), with the 10-year study certificate.

documents.name: St. John's category certificates (Annexures 13 to 16), if you apply under them
documents.detail: The baptism certificate must be in English, or come with an English transcript attested by the Bishop.

documents.name: Parent's service or home-town certificates, if you claim clause d, e, f or g
documents.detail: d: your 10-year study certificate (1st to 12th standard, including the years outside Karnataka), and a certificate from DPAR, Government of Karnataka (Principal, Deputy or Under Secretary) that the parent is in the All India Service, Karnataka cadre, with the period served outside Karnataka. If the parent is a State Government employee, get it from their Head of Department or Head of Office. e: the parent's 10-year Karnataka study certificate from the head of the institution, countersigned by the BEO/DDPI (Annexure 11), and the employer's certificate that the parent declared Karnataka as home town on joining and is transferable anywhere in India, countersigned by the employer's competent authority. f: Parliament Secretariat certificate that the parent is or was an MP elected from Karnataka, and your 10-year study certificate including the years in New Delhi. g: the parent's Karnataka home-town declaration made on joining. For serving defence personnel it comes from the respective branch or integrated HQ of MoD (officers) or the Record Office (JCOs/OR). For ex-servicemen it comes from the district Joint or Deputy Director, countersigned by the Director, Department of Sainik Welfare and Resettlement, Bengaluru.

documents.name: Any additional documents KEA notifies
documents.detail: KEA or the Entrance Test Committee can ask for more documents at any time through a notification on its website.

documents.name: Two sets of photocopies of everything
documents.detail: Don't bring laminated marks cards or certificates: KEA won't verify them, and you can't continue to seat allotment.

documents.name: Choice printout, fee receipt and verification slip (before Round 2)
documents.detail: Choice 2 candidates bring the fee receipt. All eligible Round 2 participants bring all originals including Annexures 1, 2 and 7, and one set of photocopies.

admission.title: Admission is provisional
admission.detail: Join the college with the required undertakings by the due date on your admission order, or the seat is cancelled automatically. Admission stays subject to approval by the Government, apex bodies and the university.

admission.title: False documents: seat cancelled and prosecution
admission.detail: If any information or document is false, fake or tampered, your seat is cancelled at any point during the course, all fees are forfeited, and KEA will start criminal proceedings. You may be debarred from future exams and counselling, and blacklisting and cancellation of your council registration may be recommended.

admission.title: No changes after you apply
admission.detail: KEA won't edit any information you entered, including name, category, PwD status, qualification and date of birth, under any circumstances. Keep a hard copy of your application until counselling ends.

admission.title: Certificates can be checked any time
admission.detail: KEA, DME, the Government and RGUHS can verify the authenticity of your certificates at any time, and KEA can withdraw any admission that doesn't meet the eligibility rules.

admission.title: Attend verification yourself
admission.detail: You must attend document verification in person. No one can represent you. Verification takes time, and requests to be verified before your scheduled time won't be entertained, so plan your return journey. You can bring water, food and medicines.

admission.title: Use your own mobile number and email
admission.detail: KEA sends updates only to the mobile number and email you registered. It isn't responsible if you miss information because of a wrong number. Check the KEA website often.

admission.title: Don't share counselling content
admission.detail: Sharing any content of this counselling with others, including on WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter or other social media, breaches the non-disclosure agreement and can lead to penal action and cancellation of your candidature.

admission.title: Beware of touts
admission.detail: Nobody can guarantee a PG seat through KEA. Seats go by NEET merit and your options. Report anyone claiming otherwise to keauthority-ka@nic.in.

admission.title: MDS: your BDS aggregate is checked
admission.detail: The aggregate BDS percentage you gave in your NEET-MDS 2026 form is verified against your originals at admission. If it was used to break a rank tie and turns out to be wrong, your NEET-MDS 2026 candidature is cancelled.

admission.title: The Rules prevail
admission.detail: The bulletin is subject to the Karnataka PG entrance test Rules, 2006 and government orders. If they differ, the Rules prevail, and the decision of the Government or Entrance Test Committee is final.

admission.title: Appeal within 15 days
admission.detail: If you're aggrieved by an order of KEA's Executive Director, you can appeal within 15 days to the Principal Secretary, Higher Education Department, Government of Karnataka, whose decision is final. Disputes fall under the High Court of Karnataka.

ladder.stage: Cancel a Round 1 seat after admission
ladder.window: Up to one day before Round 2 counselling (as notified)

ladder.stage: Allotted a clinical seat in Round 2 but don't join
ladder.window: By the last date of joining for Round 2
ladder.fees: Pay ₹1,50,000 for a medical or dental degree, or ₹60,000 for a diploma. This applies to every candidate, including in-service candidates.
ladder.otherConsequence: You can't take part in further rounds or admissions that academic year.

ladder.stage: Cancel after Round 2's last joining date
ladder.window: Up to one day before the mop-up round
ladder.fees: Penalty of ₹7,00,000 for a medical or dental clinical degree, or ₹3,00,000 for a clinical diploma.

ladder.stage: Cancel or surrender after the mop-up round
ladder.window: After the mop-up round, in person at the Directorate of Medical Education
ladder.fees: Penalty of ₹18,00,000 for a medical clinical degree or diploma, or ₹6,00,000 for a dental degree or diploma, and the fees paid are forfeited. Pre-clinical seats (Anatomy, Physiology, Biochemistry, Forensic Medicine): ₹1,00,000 and fees forfeited. Para-clinical seats (Pharmacology, Pathology, Microbiology, Community Medicine): ₹2,00,000 for a degree or ₹75,000 for a diploma (written in words as seventy thousand; confirm with KEA), and tuition forfeited.
ladder.otherConsequence: You're ineligible for further rounds of admission, including names-list admission.
ladder.note: The ₹75,000 para-clinical diploma penalty is written in words as 'Rupees Seventy thousand only' on p43.

ladder.stage: Leave the course before completing it
ladder.window: After the last date of admission for the year
ladder.fees: Bond penalty of ₹10,00,000 for a degree or ₹4,00,000 for a diploma. Pre-clinical seats: ₹1,00,000 and fees forfeited. Para-clinical seats: ₹1,00,000 for a degree or ₹75,000 for a diploma, and tuition forfeited.
ladder.otherConsequence: You also pay the entire course fee and stipend to the college.

rules.title: 3-year bar on new PG seats
rules.detail: If you're a regular (non-in-service) candidate and cancel or surrender a PG seat after the last date of admissions, you can't take a management quota or any other PG seat for three years. If you fail to join after allotment, the same bar and disciplinary action apply, and this appears to cover in-service candidates too.

rules.title: You can't rejoin a seat you gave up
rules.detail: Whether you're a regular or in-service candidate, and whether you cancel before or after the last date, you aren't permitted to rejoin the cancelled or surrendered seat.

rules.title: Surrender only through KEA or DME
rules.detail: Don't surrender a seat at the college. Surrender only at KEA, and after the last date of admission, only at the Directorate of Medical Education.

rules.title: In-service candidates: recovery from salary
rules.detail: If an in-service candidate leaves the course, doesn't progress, doesn't finish on time, or fails to resume duty after deputation or at any time within ten years of finishing, the Government can recover everything spent (pay, allowances, stipend, DA, tuition fee) with penalty and interest from salary.

rules.title: Originals are released only after the penalty
rules.detail: If you surrender after results, your original documents are returned only after you pay the penalty.

bond.appliesTo: Candidates taking Government seats, including All India Quota, in PG medical courses
bond.placeOfService: Any location in Karnataka decided by the Government of Karnataka, if the Government wants you to serve
bond.note: The bond text covers PG medical courses. The bulletin doesn't say whether MDS Government seats carry one.

rules.title: One year of compulsory service after PG
rules.detail: Everyone admitted to a PG Medical degree or diploma in a government, private or deemed college, under any quota, must do one year of compulsory service in a Government hospital in an urban area after finishing, under the Karnataka Compulsory Service Act, 2012. You get only temporary registration until you complete it. Candidates who already did compulsory rural service after MBBS are exempt.
rules.note: Titled 'Compulsory rural service' but the text says 'Government hospital in urban area'. Quoted as written.

rules.title: Two sureties and originals held
rules.detail: The three-year undertaking needs two sureties with self-attested PAN and Aadhaar copies, and you and they are jointly and severally bound to pay the ₹50 lakh / ₹25 lakh penalty. Your original documents stay with the institution and are returned only after you pay any penalty.

rules.title: In-service: 10 years of service
rules.detail: In-service candidates sign a bond at admission to serve the Government for at least ten years.

instructions: KEA office and document verification venue: KEA, 18th Cross, Sampige Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru.
KEA also has a chatbot (kea-bot.com), the KEA app, the KEA Vikasana YouTube channel and X (@KEA_KARNATAKA).

Report touts offering seats to keauthority-ka@nic.in.
